The release where Atrium learns to run more than one account, tells you when an agent needs you, and lets you take a kill back. Plus a first run that gets you to your first agent without opening the README, and a rebuilt settings panel for everything after.

## Breaking

**On modern terminals, `ctrl-m` / `ctrl-i` / `ctrl-h` / `ctrl-[` are no longer the same keys as `enter` / `tab` / `backspace` / `esc`.**

Atrium moved to Bubble Tea v2, which asks the terminal to disambiguate them unconditionally — there is no opt-out. On Ghostty, Kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, foot, iTerm2, Rio and modifyOtherKeys-capable xterms, they now arrive as distinct keys.

- **If you press keys, nothing changes.** No Atrium binding relied on the old conflation, so nothing you press today means something different.
- **If you script Atrium, check your macros.** A macro that sends `ctrl-m` to mean Enter must now send Enter — likewise `ctrl-i` for Tab, `ctrl-h` for Backspace, `ctrl-[` for Esc.
- **Esc is instant now.** It takes effect immediately instead of waiting out an escape-sequence timeout.

## Highlights

### Getting started

- **Guided first run.** A new install walks you through picking an agent, detects which CLIs are actually on your PATH, and hands you a board with one clear next step — instead of a blank screen and a README.
- **Antigravity joins the roster.** Google's `agy` CLI is a first-class agent alongside Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and Aider, with per-session account routing of its own (Linux, via `bwrap`). Atrium also re-scans your PATH at startup, so a CLI you install later shows up without a reconfigure.
- **New sessions come up ready to work.** Name gitignored paths in `link_paths` — `node_modules`, a virtualenv, a build cache — and Atrium symlinks them into each new worktree instead of copying, so a session's tooling resolves on the first command and a large dependency tree isn't duplicated per agent. The sharing is the point: a linked path is your real checkout under another name, so an agent that runs `npm install` or deletes the tree changes it for you and for every other session at once. That's right for the sessions that only read it, and wrong for the one whose whole job is upgrading dependencies — so that choice is now per session. The new-session form grows a **Dependencies** row wherever `link_paths` is configured: leave it on *shared* for the usual case, switch it to *isolated* for the upgrade session, and that worktree gets none of the links. Whatever it installs is its own, your checkout is untouched, and it dies with the session. Pair it with a `repo_scripts` setup script and the isolated session installs itself on the way up.

### Accounts

- **Multiple Claude, GitHub and Antigravity accounts, managed in-app.** Add accounts, see which login each one is *really* signed in as, group the session list by account, and route each worktree's `gh` to its own credentials. Account pools rotate work across available logins, and Atrium refuses to launch a session onto the wrong Claude login rather than quietly billing it.

### Knowing what needs you

- **You get told when an agent needs you.** A bell, an OSC 9 notification that survives SSH, or a desktop notification when a background session finishes a turn or blocks on a prompt. Notifications stay quiet while you're looking at Atrium, a blocked session outranks a finished one, and any session can be muted.
- **Sharper status.** Atrium tells an agent waiting on a sub-agent apart from one that's done, holds "working" from a version-independent hook heartbeat, and keeps a bounded history of every status transition.
- **PR state on the row.** The PR chip carries CI shape as well as colour — `#12✓` passing, `#12✗` failing, `#12•` pending — and links straight to the PR. After a merge, Atrium offers to clean up the finished session instead of leaving it parked with its worktree still on disk.

### Working the board

- **Command palette.** `ctrl-k` finds any action by name and runs it. Actions the current selection can't take are dimmed with the reason, so the palette explains itself instead of just failing.
- **A real settings panel.** Two panes, ten categories, search, per-setting reset and deep links — with agent profiles editable without leaving the app. Most settings apply live.
- **The board bends to the task.** Layout presets on `\`, a draggable divider with finer width steps, project section headers, reorderable sessions and account clusters, and new filter predicates: `effort:`, `model:`, `mode:`, `account:`, `note:`, plus bare `muted` and `unread`.
- **Scroll an attached session from the keyboard.** `shift-↑`/`↓` for a line, `shift-pgup`/`pgdn` for a page, then copy-mode search and selection — all bound prefix-free, so it works without touching your `~/.tmux.conf`.
- **An empty board worth looking at.** Five generative splash patterns — rain, tunnel, ripple, galaxy, aurora — rotating per launch, a full-window screensaver, and an off switch.

### Prompts and dispatch

- **Prompts queue instead of getting lost.** Queued prompts are a persisted FIFO with delivery acks and an overlay to review or cancel them, submitted prompts are kept for reuse, and a new-session draft you escaped out of survives a restart.
- **Comment on a diff line.** Annotate a line or a range in the diff tab and queue it straight to the agent.
- **Fan one prompt across profiles.** N-variant spawn starts the same prompt on several agents at once, so you can compare what comes back.
- **Reasoning effort, per session.** Choose the effort level when you create a session, see it as a chip on the row, and filter by it with `effort:`.
- **Shift+Enter is a real newline now.** In the new-session prompt and the quick-send box, Shift+Enter inserts a line break while Enter still sends — no `/terminal-setup` remap, no configuration — on any terminal that speaks the keyboard protocol (Ghostty, Kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, foot, iTerm2 and friends). `Ctrl+J` still works everywhere, and Alt+Enter still works too. The hint only promises `⇧↵` once your terminal has actually said it will deliver it, so where Atrium can't be sure it names `⌃J` instead — and the new-session form drops that clause on a narrow terminal, so the quick-send box is the one to read the answer off. `atrium doctor` explains what it could and couldn't tell.

### Safety nets

- **A kill you can take back.** `ctrl-x` used to be the one unrecoverable action — worktree removed, branch force-deleted. It's now undoable, and Atrium warns first about commits a delete would actually discard.
- **A session cap that fits the host.** By default Atrium derives a soft cap from your CPU threads and warns once when a create or a resume crosses it. Set `max_sessions` for a hard cap on every session, or `0` to opt out.

### Beyond the TUI

- **A programmable surface.** `atrium ls --json`, `atrium peek` and `atrium send` let another agent — or a script — drive the board.
- **Atrium shows up in your terminal's chrome.** The window title and taskbar carry the fleet's state, copies reach your clipboard over SSH via OSC 52, branch and PR text is clickable via OSC 8, and the hint bar is clickable — with an off-switch for mouse capture when you'd rather your terminal keep its own selection.
- **A command log.** Every tmux, git and gh command Atrium runs is recorded and viewable, so a surprising outcome leaves a trail.
- **Agents know where they are.** Claude sessions open with a brief naming their worktree, their branch and what Atrium owns, so an agent stops trying to manage the worktree it's living in. `atrium doctor` now checks tmux, git and gh alongside the agent CLIs.

### Under the hood

- **Rebuilt on Bubble Tea v2.** The whole rendering and input stack moved to Bubble Tea v2 and Lip Gloss v2, and deliberately looks the same: eighteen full-frame snapshots at two terminal sizes came through the migration byte for byte. Colour is the one exception, and it got *more* accurate — Lip Gloss v1's truecolor round-trip dropped the low bit on 24 of 256 channel values, so Atrium now renders the palette it actually specifies. Home and End decode natively, Esc responds immediately (see Breaking), and synchronized output is negotiated with terminals that advertise it. It is also what the adaptive light/dark theming and the Shift+Enter newline above are built on.

## Fixes

- **Prompts land.** New-session and queued prompts go through a verified, closed-loop send that confirms the text arrived and submitted — including long multi-line prompts Claude collapses into a paste chip, and prompts sitting behind a trust or setup screen, which are now surfaced instead of silently stalling.
- **Sessions survive the edges.** In-flight sessions are no longer orphaned by a signal shutdown or a force-quit, zombie tmux clients are reaped, lost sessions recover safely and visibly, and a second Atrium on the same data dir is refused rather than left to clobber the first.
- **Attach and detach behave.** Returning from an attach refreshes the whole list immediately, a tmux client exiting mid-attach returns you to the TUI, raw-mode failures are surfaced rather than leaving detach mysteriously broken, and prompt delivery and auto-accept keep running while you're attached.
- **The board stays responsive.** tmux, git and gh calls are off the update thread, confirm actions — push, merge, PR, pause, resume — run off the UI thread, and work that does take a while says what it's doing while it runs.
- **Auto-accept stops guessing wrong.** It no longer Enter-approves Claude selection menus, Codex and Gemini quoted literals, or anything but the confirmation shapes it actually recognizes.
- **Agent detection keeps up with Claude.** Busy, permission-dialog, trust-gate and footer detection are re-anchored to markers that survive Claude's reflows and rewordings, and keyed on the halves you can't rebind.
- **The UI stops shearing.** The paused view wraps instead of tearing, notices no longer reflow the layout in clean mode, the hint bar gets its row back when a modal closes, long descriptions wrap instead of clipping, the create form fits an 80-column terminal — every hint, refusal and verdict in it renders whole rather than losing its tail — and glyphs render on plain fonts without a Nerd Font.
- **The new-session form tells you the truth about your target.** Pointing it at a path that isn't a directory no longer describes it as a direct session, and a batch it refuses now explains why in full instead of trailing off mid-sentence.
- **Sessions start where they should.** Window names are sanitized for tmux 3.7, a resumed session with no conversation starts blank, and a new session's cursor isn't stolen when its async start completes.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZviBaratz/atrium/main/install.sh | bash
```

Or with Go — note this builds from source and reports a `dev` version (the
script installs the version-stamped, self-updating release binary):

```bash
go install github.com/ZviBaratz/atrium@v0.9.0
```

Already running Atrium? `atrium update` verifies and swaps in the new binary; running sessions are undisturbed and the new version takes effect on the next launch.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/ZviBaratz/atrium/compare/v0.8.0...v0.9.0

This is a 0.x release — APIs and behavior may change.
